backlog.title: Phase 1 — File-disjoint staging fast-path (G29, FR-M13/FR-M14)
backlog.description: Implement the v3.2 file-disjoint staging fast-path: when the planner's partition is pairwise file-disjoint, stage each concept deterministically with `git add` (no stager agent), freeze all trees up front, run all N message generations concurrently, and publish in strict CAS order. A shared file falls back transparently to the existing tooled-stager runLoop for the whole run. The fast-path is automatic and configuration-free. Spec is final (spec/01-product.md §9.14 FR-M13/M14, §13.6.3 addendum, G29); code does not exist yet (grep-confirmed zero hits). All §13.6.3/§20.2 invariants are preserved on both paths.

milestones.title: Implement + test the fast-path
milestones.description: Land the fast-path as a sibling function to runLoop in internal/decompose/decompose.go, wire a one-line gate in Decompose(), and add a regression suite. runLoop is preserved verbatim as the shared-file fallback. The arbiter/planner/message roles are unchanged and consume the fast-path output without modification.

subtasks.title: isFileDisjoint gate — pure predicate + unit test
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/019_2f5621db4d2b/architecture/system_context.md sections 4 & 6, and spec_requirements.md. The gate is a PURE function (no I/O, deterministic set-membership test). Authoritative req: spec/01-product.md §9.14 FR-M13 ('pairwise file-disjoint ... a set-membership test over the planner files; adds no configuration') and spec/03-generation.md §13.6.3 addendum. No fast-path code exists yet (grep for disjoint|fastpath|isFileDisjoint across internal/decompose/ confirmed zero hits).
2. INPUT: []prompt.PlannerCommit — the planner output Commits field (internal/prompt/planner.go:83-87). Each PlannerCommit has Files []string (the disjointness-test input and the git-add pathspec source).
3. LOGIC: Add a pure function `func isFileDisjoint(concepts []prompt.PlannerCommit) bool` in internal/decompose/decompose.go (place near runLoop, decompose.go:456). Iterate every concept's Files; track a map[string]int occurrence count; return true iff NO path's count exceeds 1. A concept with empty Files does NOT disqualify (it shares no path — it stages nothing and hits FR-M8 empty-skip downstream). A single path appearing in >=2 concepts returns false (disqualifies the fast-path for the WHOLE run — FR-M13 is explicit). Deterministic, no I/O. Write unit tests in decompose_test.go: pairwise-disjoint (>=3 concepts, distinct Files) -> true; one shared file in two concepts -> false; a concept with empty Files among disjoint others -> true; all-empty Files -> true; single concept -> true. No git/state mutation, no mocking needed.
4. OUTPUT: isFileDisjoint(concepts) bool, consumed by P1.M1.T1.S4 (the Decompose dispatch gate).
5. DOCS: none — internal pure predicate; no user-facing/config/API surface change.

subtasks.title: runLoopFastPath — serial deterministic staging sweep + tree freeze + FR-M1c + FR-M8 empty-skip
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/019_2f5621db4d2b/architecture/system_context.md sections 2-3 and git_primitives.md. runLoop at internal/decompose/decompose.go:456 is the REFERENCE implementation to mirror. git.Add(ctx, paths []string) ALREADY EXISTS (interface git.go:158, impl git.go:1339 — stages adds/mods/deletions for whole paths, nil-safe on empty; PRD's ':1332' citation is off by 7 = the doc-comment start) — call deps.Git.Add(ctx, concept.Files) directly, NO wrapper. freezeSnapshot (stager.go:141), verifyFreezeSubset (stager.go:168). The index is ALREADY reset to baseTree by Decompose step 3 (FreezeWorkingTree at decompose.go:189) — do NOT re-reset; prevTree := baseTree baseline is identical to runLoop (decompose.go:459). CRITICAL: the staging sweep MUST run strictly serially — gitRunner has NO in-process index lock (git_primitives.md CRITICAL section); Add/WriteTree mutate .git/index.
2. INPUT: ctx, deps Deps, concepts []prompt.PlannerCommit, baseTree, tStart, preRunHEAD string, isUnborn bool (same args as runLoop, decompose.go:456). concepts come from out.Commits (decompose.go:215).
3. LOGIC: Create `func runLoopFastPath(ctx context.Context, deps Deps, concepts []prompt.PlannerCommit, baseTree, tStart, preRunHEAD string, isUnborn bool) ([]CommitResult, []ChainEntry, error)` in decompose.go as a SIBLING to runLoop (do NOT modify runLoop — it stays byte-identical as the shared-file fallback). This subtask implements the SERIAL STAGING PHASE only: (a) compute tStartPaths via deps.Git.DiffTreeNames(ctx, baseTree, tStart) exactly as runLoop (decompose.go:465) — the FR-M1c baseline. (b) prevTree := baseTree. (c) Serial loop over each concept i in order: deps.Git.Add(ctx, concepts[i].Files) (per-path add — stages the concept's whole paths); treeI, err := freezeSnapshot(ctx, deps); on err return (commits-so-far, nil, err) partial. (d) verifyFreezeSubset(ctx, deps, baseTree, tStart, tStartPaths, i, concepts[i].Title, treeI) — FR-M1c runs on EVERY tree unchanged (whole-path adds of T_start content pass trivially but it MUST still run); on violation there is no in-flight message yet, so return (partial commits, nil, vErr) NON-RESCUE mirroring runLoop's verify handling. (e) FR-M8 empty-skip: if treeI == prevTree skip concept i (no message, no commit), log at deps.Verbose, keep prevTree unchanged, continue; else append stagedConcept{idx: i, tree: treeI, prevTree: prevTree} to a collected slice and set prevTree = treeI. After the sweep every non-skipped tree[i] is FROZEN — this is the FR-M14 precondition ('every tree[i] frozen before any message starts').
4. OUTPUT: runLoopFastPath skeleton + serial staging sweep producing a []stagedConcept slice. Define the struct: type stagedConcept struct { idx int; tree, prevTree string }. The full function still returns ([]CommitResult, []ChainEntry, error); P1.M1.T1.S3 completes it with the concurrent phase. runLoop stays UNCHANGED.
5. DOCS: none — internal function.

subtasks.title: runLoopFastPath — concurrent message generation + CAS-ordered publish + FR-M12 failure isolation
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/019_2f5621db4d2b/architecture/system_context.md section 3 and git_primitives.md CRITICAL CONCURRENCY. REUSE existing primitives — do NOT reimplement: generateMessage (message.go:70 — tree-to-tree diff, read-only w.r.t. index, returns *generate.RescueError on failure), publishCommit (message.go:232 — CommitTree + UpdateRefCAS, returns *generate.CASError on CAS fail), buildCommitResult (decompose.go:760), drainMsg (decompose.go:617 — nil-safe, drains ONE buffered(1) channel), signal.SetSnapshot (signal.go:204) / ClearSnapshot (signal.go:224). Concurrency is SAFE here because message goroutines reason over tree-to-tree diffs only and never touch the live .git/index (generateMessage's contract); commit-tree + update-ref also never touch the index. The update-ref CAS MUST serialize in order (FR-M7) — the publish loop is the serialization point. No concurrency cap (FR-M14; max_commits default 12 bounds N — do NOT add a config key).
2. INPUT: the []stagedConcept slice (frozen tree[i] + prevTree + concept idx) produced by P1.M1.T1.S2; plus ctx, deps, tStart, preRunHEAD, isUnborn in runLoopFastPath scope.
3. LOGIC: Complete runLoopFastPath's CONCURRENT PHASE: (a) launch ALL N (non-skipped) message generations concurrently using the buffered(1)-channel launch() pattern from runLoop (decompose.go:475-482) — each goroutine calls generateMessage(ctx, deps, sc.prevTree, sc.tree); arm signal.SetSnapshot(sc.tree, parentSHA, empty) per in-flight message (rescue coverage, as runLoop does at decompose.go:605). (b) PUBLISH STRICTLY IN CAS ORDER (FR-M7): consume results in concept order; commit[0] parent = preRunHEAD (or root if isUnborn); commit[i] parent = newSHA[i-1]; reuse publishCommit + buildCommitResult + ChainEntry{SHA, Tree, Message, Parent} accumulation exactly as runLoop's publish closure (decompose.go:488-527). signal.ClearSnapshot() after each drain. (c) FR-M12 per-concept failure isolation on the concurrent path: on a *generate.RescueError at position i -> publish commits 0..i-1 (already landed), print generate.FormatRescueMulti(...) naming concept i, DRAIN the remaining in-flight message channels (i+1..N-1) to avoid goroutine leaks, return *DecomposeRescueError carrying partial commits (same partial-commits-stand semantics as runLoop). On a *generate.CASError during publish -> print ce.Error(), drain remaining, return ce (prior commits stand). GENERALIZE drainMsg from a single channel to a slice (or loop it over the remaining channels) — the ONLY behavioral difference from runLoop is that 'drain remaining' covers N-i-1 channels instead of 1. Return (commits, chainData, nil) on full success. The arbiter (runArbiterPhase) runs UNCHANGED after either path — do NOT touch arbiter.go/chain.go.
4. OUTPUT: complete runLoopFastPath returning ([]CommitResult, []ChainEntry, error) in the SAME shapes runLoop returns, so the post-loop code in Decompose (arbiter gate at decompose.go:248-268, rereadFinalCommits, DecomposeResult assembly) is shared and unchanged.
5. DOCS: none — internal function.

subtasks.title: Decompose() dispatch wiring — gate isFileDisjoint -> runLoopFastPath else runLoop
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/019_2f5621db4d2b/architecture/system_context.md section 1. The dispatch site is internal/decompose/decompose.go:228-238 — insert BETWEEN the runSingleShortcut block (ends :230) and the runLoop call (:237). Variables in scope at that point: ctx, deps, out prompt.PlannerOutput (out.Single==false, len(out.Commits)>=2), baseTree, tStart, preRunHEAD, isUnborn. The arbiter phase + rereadFinalCommits + DecomposeResult assembly that follow the runLoop call site are SHARED and must remain unchanged.
2. INPUT: isFileDisjoint(out.Commits) from P1.M1.T1.S1; runLoopFastPath(...) from P1.M1.T1.S3; runLoop(...) unchanged.
3. LOGIC: Replace the single `commits, chainData, err := runLoop(ctx, deps, out.Commits, baseTree, tStart, preRunHEAD, isUnborn)` line (decompose.go:237) with a gate: if isFileDisjoint(out.Commits) { commits, chainData, err = runLoopFastPath(ctx, deps, out.Commits, baseTree, tStart, preRunHEAD, isUnborn) } else { commits, chainData, err = runLoop(ctx, deps, out.Commits, baseTree, tStart, preRunHEAD, isUnborn) }. Log the gate's decision (which path taken) at deps.Verbose. Everything after (arbiter phase, rereadFinalCommits, DecomposeResult assembly) is shared and unchanged. runLoop stays the shared-file fallback, byte-identical. No new config key or CLI flag (FR-M13: adds no configuration).
4. OUTPUT: Decompose() now dispatches disjoint partitions to the fast-path and shared-file partitions to runLoop. Identical observable commits + safety guarantees on both paths.
5. DOCS: none — internal dispatch; no CLI/config surface.

subtasks.title: Fast-path regression suite in decompose_test.go (disjoint/fallback/concurrency/CAS/isolation/skip/freeze)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/019_2f5621db4d2b/architecture/system_context.md section 6 (stager seam), spec_requirements.md sections §20.2/§20.5, and git_primitives.md. The test substrate is the existing internal/decompose/decompose_test.go (temp-repo + internal/stubtest stub planner/stager/arbiter). deps.stager (roles.go ~88-95) is the test seam: nil in prod; inject a stub that t.Fatal('stager must not be called on the fast-path') to assert the fast-path never invokes it. The fast-path is unreachable from invokeStager by construction (invokeStager <- invokeStagerRetry <- runLoop only). Authoritative invariants: spec/06-reliability.md §20.2 (concept isolation, T_start completeness, start-of-run freeze FR-M1b, atomic HEAD) and §20.5 (e2e must-cover set).
2. INPUT: The completed runLoopFastPath + dispatch (P1.M1.T1.S4); the stub planner/stager/arbiter scaffolding already in decompose_test.go.
3. LOGIC: Add a runLoopFastPath coverage set to decompose_test.go (extend the existing stub suite; TDD per SOW §3 — write failing test, implement, pass). Cases (from PRD §5 + spec §20.2/§20.5): (1) Disjoint -> N commits, stager NEVER invoked: stub planner returns >=3 concepts with pairwise-disjoint Files; inject a stager stub that fails if called; assert exactly N commits land, each commit's diff-tree (vs parent) == exactly that concept's Files (concept isolation §20.2), the chain parents correctly, all of T_start committed (drive BOTH sub-cases: frozen leftover empty -> arbiter skipped; AND arbiter folds unclaimed paths). (2) Shared file -> fallback to tooled stager for the WHOLE run: one path in two concepts' Files; assert the tooled stager stub IS invoked for every concept (existing runLoop path) and the resulting commits match the pre-fast-path behavior. (3) Concurrency is real: N message goroutines overlap in time (each stub message records a start/end timestamp into a shared slice under a mutex; assert the intervals pairwise overlap, not strictly serial) — guards against a future refactor silently re-serializing. (4) CAS-ordered publication under concurrency: stub message i sleeps proportional to N-i so later concepts finish FIRST; assert the final chain is strictly ordered preRunHEAD -> c0 -> c1 -> ... and each parent is correct. (5) FR-M12 failure isolation on the fast-path: (a) stub message at position 1 returns a *generate.RescueError-inducing output -> assert commits 0 landed, the rescue message names concept 1, and the remaining in-flight messages were drained (no goroutine leak); (b) stub publish at position 1 trips a CAS failure (move HEAD mid-publish) -> assert prior commits stand and the run aborts. (6) FR-M8 empty-skip on the fast-path: a concept whose Files stage nothing (empty Files, or paths not in T_start) -> tree[i]==prevTree -> skipped, no empty commit, run continues. (7) FR-M1c still guards fast-path trees: assert verifyFreezeSubset is CALLED once per non-skipped concept (count via a counting git wrapper or a seam) so the guard is provably wired. (8) tooled_flags-less provider succeeds on a disjoint tree (G29 side effect): a stub stager manifest with empty tooled_flags (opencode/qwen-code shape) on a DISJOINT partition -> the run SUCCEEDS via the fast-path (no stager needed); on a SHARED-file partition -> falls back and surfaces the existing 'cannot serve as a stager' error (unchanged). (9) Start-of-run freeze (FR-M1b): write a sentinel file to the working tree after T_start is frozen and before the run completes; assert it lands in NO fast-path commit and remains in the working tree post-run. Run the full `go test ./internal/decompose/... ./internal/git/... ./internal/config/...` green.
4. OUTPUT: a green test suite covering the fast-path's new behaviors + its fallback, in decompose_test.go. Proves the arbiter consumes the fast-path's output without modification.
5. DOCS: none — tests.
